title: Healthcare & Medical Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to protect your medical data, ensure HIPAA compliance, and secure health apps. Safeguard your healthcare privacy today.
intro: Your medical information is among your most sensitive personal data. This comprehensive checklist helps you protect your health records, secure medical apps, and understand your HIPAA rights to maintain complete healthcare privacy.

items.task: Request and review HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices from all healthcare providers
items.why: Understanding your rights under HIPAA helps you know how your medical information can be used and shared by healthcare providers.
items.howTo: Contact each healthcare provider's office and request their current Notice of Privacy Practices. Read through to understand your rights to access, amend, and restrict use of your health information.

items.task: Request minimum necessary disclosure for all medical information sharing
items.why: HIPAA requires providers to limit disclosures to the minimum necessary, but you can explicitly request this protection.
items.howTo: Submit written requests to your healthcare providers asking them to limit disclosures to only the minimum necessary information for each specific purpose.

items.task: Secure all patient portal accounts with strong passwords and 2FA
items.why: Patient portals contain complete medical histories and are prime targets for hackers seeking valuable health data.
items.howTo: Enable two-factor authentication on all patient portal accounts. Use unique, strong passwords and consider using a password manager to generate and store them securely.

items.task: Set secure communication preferences with healthcare providers
items.why: Unsecured communications like regular email or voicemail can expose your medical information to unauthorized parties.
items.howTo: Request that providers only communicate through secure patient portals or encrypted email. Avoid discussing sensitive medical information over regular phone lines when possible.

items.task: Audit all health and fitness apps for privacy policies and data sharing
items.why: Many health apps aren't covered by HIPAA and may sell your health data to third parties without clear disclosure.
items.howTo: Review privacy policies of all health-related apps. Look for data sharing practices, third-party partnerships, and opt-out options. Delete apps with poor privacy practices.

items.task: Restrict health app permissions to essential functions only
items.why: Health apps often request excessive permissions that allow access to contacts, location, and other sensitive data beyond their core function.
items.howTo: Go to your device's app permissions settings and review each health app. Disable location tracking, contact access, and other unnecessary permissions while keeping core health functions enabled.

items.task: Configure privacy settings on fitness trackers and wearable devices
items.why: Fitness trackers collect detailed health and location data that can reveal personal patterns and sensitive health conditions.
items.howTo: Access your fitness tracker's companion app and privacy settings. Disable data sharing with third parties, turn off public activity sharing, and limit location tracking to when necessary.

items.task: Review and limit health data synchronization across devices and services
items.why: Automatic syncing can spread your health data across multiple platforms, increasing exposure risk and making it harder to control.
items.howTo: Check settings in Apple Health, Google Fit, and similar platforms. Disable automatic syncing with apps you don't actively use and review which apps have access to your health data.

items.task: Use private browsing for all health-related online research
items.why: Health searches can be tracked and used to build profiles about your medical conditions, potentially affecting insurance or employment.
items.howTo: Always use Incognito Browser or private browsing mode when researching health conditions, medications, or medical providers. This prevents search history from being stored locally.

items.task: Use privacy-focused search engines for medical information
items.why: Major search engines track and store your health-related searches, which can be used for targeted advertising or shared with third parties.
items.howTo: Use DuckDuckGo, Startpage, or similar privacy-focused search engines when looking up health information. These services don't track or store your search history.

items.task: Use a VPN when accessing health information online
items.why: Your internet provider and network administrators can see what health websites you visit, potentially revealing sensitive medical interests.
items.howTo: Connect to a reputable VPN service before researching health topics online. This encrypts your connection and hides your browsing activity from your internet provider.

items.task: Regularly clear browser data related to health searches
items.why: Even with private browsing, some data may be stored. Regular clearing ensures no health-related browsing traces remain on your device.
items.howTo: Clear your browser's cookies, cache, and search history weekly. Pay special attention to removing any stored passwords or autofill data for health-related websites.

items.task: Request copies of your complete medical records from all providers
items.why: Having your own copies ensures you know what information exists and can identify any inaccuracies that need correction.
items.howTo: Submit written requests to each healthcare provider for complete copies of your medical records. Most providers must respond within 30 days and can charge reasonable copying fees.

items.task: Review medical records for accuracy and request corrections
items.why: Inaccurate medical records can affect your care and may be shared inappropriately if they contain incorrect information.
items.howTo: Carefully review all medical records for errors in diagnoses, medications, allergies, or personal information. Submit written correction requests with supporting documentation to providers.

items.task: Request removal of your information from health-related data brokers
items.why: Data brokers collect and sell personal information that can include health-related data from public records and other sources.
items.howTo: Search for your information on major data broker sites and submit removal requests. Focus on brokers that specifically deal with public records that might contain health information.

items.task: Review health insurance privacy policies and claims data
items.why: Health insurers have access to detailed medical information and may share it with affiliates or for marketing purposes.
items.howTo: Read your health insurance privacy notice carefully. Request copies of your claims history and review what information is being collected. Opt out of marketing communications and data sharing where possible.
